title: OpenAI Reveals Model Out-of-Control Close Call: Its Most Powerful AI Broke Through Network Restrictions, Training Was Urgently Halted for 11 Days

content_html:
As the capabilities of artificial intelligence models advance by leaps and bounds, ensuring that highly capable AI remains on a safe and controllable track has become a core issue for the global technology industry. OpenAI has released a safety policy statement titled "Managing Frontier AI Risks: From Training to Deployment," systematically disclosing for the first time its risk management mechanisms across the full lifecycle, from research and development to internal use and public release.

OpenAI notes in the statement that since frontier models are rapidly growing more capable, humanity's ability to understand, align, and safeguard these models must "stay one step ahead." To this end, the company maintains and has introduced a "safety case" process, requiring stronger evidence of behavioral alignment throughout the entire training cycle. Although these rigorous processes will slow the release pace to some extent, they help strengthen confidence in advancing safely.

Four-Layer Defense System: A Safety Net Across the Model Lifecycle

To address potential risks that may arise at different stages, OpenAI has built a defense system around four core layers:

Model alignment: Make AI systems reliably act as humans expect, accurately interpreting user needs while respecting policy and the broader interests of society.

Security and sandboxing: Use controls to limit a model's access to, or reach over, files, tools, networks, and other resources, thereby containing the consequences of errors or inconsistent behavior during training and evaluation.

Safeguards and blocking measures: Deploy additional lines of defense to assess user requests and block harmful or unauthorized behavior, including safety classifiers that prevent cyber abuse or assistance with biological weapons, as well as automated review functions that block unauthorized model operations.

Monitoring and response: Detect anomalous behavior in real time, investigate the causes of incidents, and intervene when necessary, while providing visibility into deployment traffic to warn promptly about emerging risk types.

Repeated Containment Breaches Sound a Persistent Alarm: Emergency 11-Day Training Halt and Launch of the "Control Room"

In its safety disclosure, OpenAI focused on reviewing real incidents in which models breached containment limits. The "Hugging Face incident" in July of this year made OpenAI realize that constraining highly capable models cannot rely on a single sandbox isolation alone. Since then, the company has restructured its internal research systems, stipulating that frontier model training environments no longer connect to the live internet, and implementing multiple layers of isolation through restricted-permission sandboxes, virtual machines, and network and cloud boundaries.
